author: opt-B6

contract.sync_assumed: caller separates consecutive calls that reuse the temp storage by a block barrier
contract.sync_performed: __syncthreads inside cub::BlockRadixSort: per 4-bit pass 2 in the ranking (counters written, counters scanned), 2 in the 256-thread BlockScan of the packed counters, 2 around the exchange, one more between passes. 4 passes for bf16 (the 16 key bits of the 32-bit word), 8 for fp32 (the 32 key bits of the 64-bit word). 26 BAR.SYNC in the latency kernel (two inlined calls plus the harness's own)
contract.k_range: [1, N) at compile time, the sort is k independent, k selects how many striped ranks are stored
contract.n_range: N = Threads x IPT, IPT >= 1, N <= 32768 (BlockRadixRank's 16-bit counters), threads 128, 256 or 512 accepted, measured N 1024 to 8192 at 256 threads
contract.type_constraints: bf16 (32-bit word: twiddled key high 16, index low 16) and fp32 (64-bit word: twiddled key high 32, index low 32), int32 indices from the blocked position. Temp storage is max(9216 bytes of rank counters at 256 threads, (N + N/32) x word bytes of exchange buffer): 9216 at bf16 N 1024 and 2048, 16896 at fp32 N 2048, 33792 at bf16 N 8192, 67584 at fp32 N 8192
contract.nan_behavior: twiddled bitwise: a positive NaN orders above +inf and a negative NaN below -inf, never produced by focus-set inputs. -0.0 is folded onto +0.0 before twiddling (one compare and select for bf16, one FADD for fp32) so both zeros form one tie class ordered by index
contract.tie_break_support: inherent: the LSD radix sort over the key bits is stable and the blocked input is in index order, so equal keys come out in ascending index order. prefer_smaller_index is the same binary as not_guaranteed and measured identical to the cycle (5550.5 against 5550.8 at bf16 N 2048 k 1024). prefer_larger_index would need the inverted index sorted as well (not built)
contract.sorted_output_support: inherent at zero extra cost: slot r of the output holds rank r (key descending, index ascending). The B6 number is the sorted-output number

correctness_notes: Every cell passed the full oracle battery under both requirements (random x4 seeds, tie_heavy, sorted_asc, sorted_desc, pivot_tie, all_equal, signed_zero, inf_denorm, quantized_random, relu_quantized), the prefer_smaller_index check is the exact index set. Two batches merged: the kill cell (label kill_b3, N 2048 k 1024) and the sort-cost sweep (label sortcost, N 1024 k 512, N 4096 k 512 and 2048, N 8192 k 2048 and 4096), both against B3_tuned in the same lock section on umbriel-b200-020, source commit 971a398f42.

low_level: Per-pass cost of the stock cub::BlockRadixSort (4-bit digit, BlockRadixRank with memoized outer scan, BLOCK_SCAN_WARP_SCANS) at 256 threads, latency regime: bf16 on 32-bit words (4 passes) 1070, 1388, 2075, 3376 cycles per pass at IPT 4, 8, 16, 32 (N 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192), least squares 740 + 82 x IPT. fp32 on 64-bit words (8 passes) 1221, 1686, 2651, 4064, fit 815 + 100 x IPT. Whole calls: bf16 4279, 5550, 8068 to 8298, 13505 to 13640, fp32 9767, 13487, 21207, 32192 to 32513.

Where a pass goes: the fixed 740 to 815 cycles are the barrier chain (6 BAR.SYNC per pass at 28 cycles each plus the arrival skew of 8 warps) and the 256-thread BlockScan over 9 packed counters per thread (SHFL.UP warp scans, an aggregate round trip through shared memory, two barriers), about 2.5 times the B3 packed scan emission (T29, about 300). The per-item 82 to 100 cycles are shared-memory wavefronts summed over 8 warps, not a dependent latency: per item and pass the ranking does one LDS.U16 and one STS.U16 on the thread's counter (a chain through the aliasing counter pointers, the compiler cannot reorder item i+1's load above item i's store), the rank extraction one LDS.U16, and the exchange one scatter STS to a random rank (bank conflicts of about 3 to 4 way at 32 random addresses, padding by one word per 32 does not remove them) and one gather LDS. 8 warps x IPT x 4 to 5 accesses per pass at one wavefront per cycle is 32 to 40 x IPT cycles, the conflicts double it. At IPT 32 the per-item part is 2600 of the 3376 cycles per pass.

SASS of the bf16 N 2048 k 1024 latency kernel (B6 kernel plus its generate-only twin, two inlined sort calls): 1008 instructions, 26 BAR.SYNC, 15 SHFL.UP, 56 LDS.U16, 24 STS.U16, 96 STS, 47 LDS, 6 LDS.128, 0 ATOMS, 0 BSSY, 0 STL, 0 LDL, stack 0. The pass loop of SortBlockedToStriped is a runtime while loop over begin_bit (BRA.U), one copy of the pass body executes 4 or 8 times, so the kernel is small (B3_tuned's fp32 kernel at the same cell has 35 BAR.SYNC static and 3 passes unrolled). fp32 N 2048: 888 instructions, 32 STS.64, 16 LDS.64, 16 SHF.R.U64 for the 64-bit digit extraction, 16 FADD for the -0.0 fold.

Registers of the latency kernel: bf16 48, 56, 79, 128 at IPT 4, 8, 16, 32 (B3_tuned 32 to 80 at the same cells), fp32 48, 64, 112 to 115, 202 to 206 (B3_tuned 40 to 127), no spill anywhere. The 64-bit words at IPT 32 (64 registers of words plus 32 ranks plus the counters) put the fp32 N 8192 kernel at the register wall: throughput occupancy 1 block per SM against B3's 2. Throughput occupancy bf16 5, 4, 2, 2 blocks per SM at N 1024 to 8192, fp32 5, 4, 2, 1. Shared memory per block (harness total, temp storage plus the double-buffered output): bf16 13376, 17472, 20992 to 33280, 50176 to 66560 bytes, fp32 13376, 25088, 37888 to 50176, 83968 to 100352, against B3_tuned 10320 at N 2048 and 21584 to 30800 at N 8192.

Throughput (one occupancy wave, Gelem per s): bf16 114, 159, 175 to 181, 201 to 205 at N 1024 to 8192 against B3_tuned 327, 450, 521 to 559, 456 to 465 (0.35x to 0.44x). fp32 45.5, 59.4, 64.0 to 64.6, 67.3 to 67.7 against 332, 456, 418 to 471, 370 to 404 (0.14x to 0.18x). The sort's shared-memory wavefronts are the SM-wide bottleneck in both regimes, so the throughput loss matches the latency loss and does not improve with occupancy.
Canaries flat at 32.00 cycles per op and 3775 to 3777 us at both ends of every batch, oracle self-test true in every cell, no cell retried.
algorithmic: Kill cell (bf16 N 2048 k 1024, random, not_guaranteed, same lock section): B6_radix 5550 cycles against B3_tuned 2550 (2.18x slower) and B1_idx 2933 (1.89x slower, card B6_radix_b200_20261025_2). fp32: 13487 against 2509 (5.37x) and 2868 (4.71x). The card's threshold was 1.2x of the better control, so B6 misses it by 1.8x (bf16) and 4.5x (fp32). Throughput at the kill cell: bf16 159 against 450 (B3) and 342 (B1_idx) Gelem per s, fp32 59 against 456 and 337.

The sort is k-flat by construction and the ratio against B3_tuned is flat too: bf16 2.28x (N 1024 k 512), 2.18x (N 2048 k 1024), 2.10x and 2.35x (N 4096 k 512 and 2048), 2.13x and 2.22x (N 8192 k 2048 and 4096), fp32 5.02x, 5.37x, 5.03x and 6.10x, 5.02x and 6.52x. B3_tuned's scan emission (T29) is itself k-flat, so no k from N/8 to N/2 and no N from 1024 to 8192 changes the verdict. The crossover table of the card does not exist: there is no crossover.

Why a radix sort cannot win a selection cell: a radix select (B1, B3) does 2 to 4 passes of one histogram sweep over the tile with no data movement and one emission, a radix sort does 4 to 8 passes each with a ranking sweep and a full exchange of every item through shared memory. The exchange alone moves N x passes words (8192 words at bf16 N 2048, 16384 words of 8 bytes at fp32) where the select moves nothing before the emission, and even at k = N/2 the select never touches the non-selected half again after pass 1. The card's cost model charged a pass at 350 to 400 cycles (the cost of one block scan), the measured pass is 1390 (bf16, IPT 8) because a ranking pass is a scan plus two sweeps plus an exchange plus six barriers.

Pass count against the card: sorting the key bits only (begin_bit 16 of the 32-bit word, begin_bit 32 of the 64-bit word) with the index in the low bits gives 4 passes for bf16 instead of the card's 8, and the stable LSD order resolves ties by index without sorting the index bits (T55). The halved pass count does not save the approach: 4 x 1390 is still 2.18x the select.

Sorted-output premium through this family, for the phase 3b pass (B6 output is sorted at zero extra cost, so the premium over B3_tuned's unsorted selection is the whole gap): bf16 2400 cycles at N 1024 k 512, 3000 at N 2048 k 1024, 4640 at N 4096 k 2048, 7490 at N 8192 k 4096, fp32 7820, 10980, 17730, 27240. Against the alternative route of selecting with B3_tuned and post-sorting the k selected words with the same BlockRadixSort (the sort of k words at 256 threads is the N = k row of this card, keys of the selected items assumed available): at k = N/2 the full sort wins for bf16 by 5 to 19 percent (N 2048: 5550 against 2550 + 4279 = 6829, N 4096: 8068 against 3427 + 5550 = 8977, N 8192: 13640 against 6154 + 8068 = 14222) because the per-pass fixed cost dominates at small IPT, and at k = N/4 the post-sort route wins (N 4096 k 1024: 8068 against 3427 + 4279 = 7706, N 8192 k 2048: 13505 against 6328 + 5550 = 11878). For fp32 the post-sort route wins at every k (N 2048 k 1024: 13487 against 2509 + 9767 = 12276, N 4096 k 2048: 21207 against 3476 + 13487 = 16963), the 64-bit word sort grows faster with IPT. The post-sort route additionally needs the selected keys (a gather from a shared copy of the tile or B3's candidate buffer), unmeasured, so the real premium of that route is higher than these sums.

prefer_smaller_index costs nothing: identical binary, cycles within 0.01 percent in every pair, the exact oracle passes on tie_heavy (1.1 to 10.4 ties at the k-th key on the bf16 cells) and signed_zero (2k zeros of both signs) through the -0.0 fold and the stability of the sort.
negative: Sort then truncate under not_guaranteed is dead at every measured cell: 2.1x to 2.4x behind B3_tuned and 1.9x behind B1_idx for bf16, 5.0x to 6.5x and 4.7x for fp32, at k from N/8 to N/2 and N 1024 to 8192, in latency and worse in throughput (0.35x to 0.44x and 0.14x to 0.18x of B3_tuned). The card's cheapest kill experiment closed the approach in one batch and the sort-cost sweep confirmed there is no crossover anywhere in the block focus range.

The crossover table, the partial-sort variant (at most the last exchange's non-selected items, a few percent of one pass out of 4 to 8) and the 512-thread form of the plan's item 2 were not built: none of them can recover a factor of 2.2 (bf16) or 5.4 (fp32). The 512-thread form would halve the per-item part of the pass at N 8192 (about 1.5x on the sort) and still leave it 1.4x behind B3_tuned at 256 threads.
The card's cost model (8 passes at 350 to 400 cycles, about 3000 at N 2048 bf16, 'above the select') had the right verdict for the wrong numbers: half the passes at four times the cost per pass.
surprises: The per-pass cost of the stock block radix sort grows linearly with items per thread at 82 (32-bit words) to 100 (64-bit words) cycles per item, which is 2 to 3 times what a dependent per-item chain would cost: the ranking and the exchange are shared-memory-wavefront bound across the 8 warps, so the block sort does not get cheaper per item at larger tiles the way B1's and B3's predicated sweeps do.

At k = N/2 the full sort of N bf16 words is cheaper than a selection followed by a sort of the k selected words with the same primitive (5550 against 6829 at N 2048), because the sort of 1024 words at IPT 4 still pays the 740-cycle fixed cost of every pass: the stock BlockRadixSort has no cheap regime at small tiles.

The 64-bit packed word and the 32-bit pairs sort tie at fp32 (13496 against 13398, card B6_pairs_b200_20261025_1), while the packed word beats the pairs sort by 1.24x at bf16: the u64 exchange moves the same bytes as a key exchange plus a value exchange, and the 64-bit digit extraction costs about what the pairs sort's extra barrier costs.

The sort kernels are small (888 to 1008 SASS instructions for two inlined calls at N 2048 against B3_tuned's unrolled passes) because the pass loop stays a runtime loop, and still 2.2x to 5.4x slower: instruction count says nothing about a wavefront-bound kernel.
open_questions: A custom ranking pass (per-thread register histogram of the 16 digits over IPT items, one packed block scan as in T29, a conflict-free exchange through warp-level striped layouts) could remove the counter chain and most of the scatter conflicts, but even a pass at the B3 scan's 300 cycles plus 20 per item would give about 1840 cycles at bf16 N 2048 (4 passes), 0.72x of B3_tuned's 2550: the sort is out as a selection primitive at any plausible implementation quality. It would matter only for the sorted-output pass.

The sorted-output pass (phase 3b) should compare three routes at k at least N/4: the full B6 sort (this card), B3_tuned plus a post-sort of the k selected words (the sort part is the N = k row here, the gather of the selected keys is unmeasured), and W4's merge of sorted chunk runs. For bf16 at k = N/2 the full sort is the better of the first two by 5 to 19 percent, everywhere else the post-sort route or the merge should win.

The chunk merge of M sorted runs of k (card explore 2, the DSA merge cells of WORKLOADS.md section 7) was not measured: it needs sorted inputs, which only W1, W2 and this sort produce, and it belongs with W4's sorted-input merge, whose owner should take the N 8192 k 2048 fp32 number here (32.2k to 32.5k for a full sort, B3_tuned 4935 to 6477 unsorted) as the bound a merge has to beat.

Whether cub::BlockRadixSort with RadixBits 5 to 8 (fewer passes, 17 to 129 packed counters per thread in the raking scan) moves the per-pass cost was not measured: the raking segment grows with the digit width and the fixed part of the pass is already 2.5 scans, so fewer passes at a higher fixed cost cannot reach a 2.2x gap. The hybrid block sort study (cccl-exp-perf HYBRID_BLOCK_SORT_RESULTS.md) puts the stock BlockMergeSort of 2048 fp32 keys at 11684 cycles and of pairs at 14795 on a B200 of July 2026, in the same band as this radix sort (13487 for the 64-bit word), so no CUB block sort is within reach of the select at these sizes.
